chapter_theme: The test (சோதனை): the seeker's search is completed when, having bathed in the ocean of grace and left all maya, he simply stays still; the Lord pervades all as ghee in milk, takes the heart as his temple, tests and leads the seeker, and gives him the sword of knowledge with which nothing can turn him aside.
structure_note: The chapter moves from the stillness that is the test (2635 to 2638), through the Lord's pervading and indwelling presence (2639 to 2642), to his testing and leading (2643, 2644) and the sword of knowledge given by him (2645 to 2648).

2635.reading: Our Lord, great Nandi, danced in the great bliss beyond speech, and we bathed in the ocean of grace; leaving every maya and hiding ourselves away, to stay simply still is the test.
2635.nuance: சோதனை can mean testing or searching, and some take it with சோதி (light). சும்மா இருத்தல் (simply being still) is a phrase of Tamil mystical tradition for the end of striving. அம்மா may be an exclamation or address the Mother.

2636.reading: I will join with the one who has all knowledge, who dwells close within the rare great Veda, the god of the gods, who holds the senses and has the mark beyond the five senses.
2636.nuance: பொறியுடையான் may mean master of the sense organs or the one with the spark or mark; குறி (mark, sign) beyond the senses may be his formless sign or a yogic object of meditation.

2637.reading: The world cries 'knowledge, knowledge', yet no one knows what knowledge and ignorance are; when knowledge goes beyond both knowledge and ignorance, how fine knowledge and ignorance then become!
2637.nuance: The verse plays on அறிவு and அறியாமை six times. The last line may be admiring (once both are transcended they are seen rightly) or ironic (how strange that is); the tone isn't fixed.

2638.reading: In the sign that is no sign, in the union that does not join, in the knowledge that does not know, loosened into a single mind, the path is supreme Nandi; his long grace is one; that close union which is no union may be called Sivam.
2638.nuance: The verse defines its goal only by negations (குறியாக் குறி, கூடாத கூட்டம், அறியா அறிவு, செறியாச் செறிவு). ஏகசித்தம் is the one-pointed or single mind. சிவமெனலாம் (may be called Sivam) is guarded: a name, not a description.

2639.reading: Like what moves in the wind, jaggery in the sugarcane, ghee in milk, juice in fruit and fragrance in the flower, so is our Lord; the guardian stands mingled everywhere.
2639.nuance: Each image is of something present throughout a thing but not visible in it. காலினில் ஊரும் is unclear: it may be scent carried on the wind, or the wind itself. Sengalvaraya notes Appar's பாலின் நெய்யாம் பழத்தின் இரதமாம் as a parallel.

2640.reading: Like a golden creeper that, joined with longing and seeking the Transcendent, reaches up a mountain, our Lord dwells in the mind, appearing as a form of fire.
2640.nuance: The creeper may be the devoted soul climbing toward the Lord, or Uma, the mountain's daughter, reaching Siva; the verse's subject shifts from the creeper to the Lord. விருப்பொடு கூடி (joined with longing) treats longing for the Lord as good.

2641.reading: Lord Nandi came in the space at the centre and took my inner self as his temple; as he did so I rose up saying 'my Father has come', and as I rose, Siva was within my thought.
2641.nuance: நடுவுள் வியோமம் (the space at the centre) is traditionally the space of the heart or the space between the brows; the verse doesn't say which. அகம்படி may be the inner self or the inner precinct of a temple, kept as a pun.

2642.reading: Without meanness or falsehood, seek the pure one, master of his nature, the good within penance, the one able in goodness, Nandi who dwells at the centre; he will shape you in many ways.
2642.nuance: பரிசுசெய்வான் may mean he will fit you, form you or reward you; பன்மையில் (in manyness) may be 'in many ways' or 'out of the many', marking the seeker out.

2643.reading: When he tested me he stood close behind me, and yet the Lord did not stand following there; spreading through all, the First, the Supreme beyond the supreme, my Father, stands beyond and shows that path.
2643.nuance: The first two lines seem to say opposite things (he followed me; he did not follow), which may contrast the Lord as near guide and as transcendent, or the guru and the Lord. சோதிக்கும் (tests) gives the chapter its title.

2644.reading: The thing rare even for the gods, who shows that path, is on this path like father, mother and kin; he sets those on the right path in Siva's world; this way is the nature of Nandi.
2644.nuance: சிவலோகம் (Siva's world) is the first of the graded states of release (salokam) in Siddhanta, though the verse may use it loosely for release. செவ்வழி (the straight or right path) can be read either with the seekers or with Siva's world.

2645.reading: Drawing and striking with the sword of the ford of knowledge, knowing that noble one by it and joining the Lord of the gods of gods, is what those who do not give up attachment to the many hosts have torn from them.
2645.nuance: The first three lines describe the work of knowledge; the last line, பறிவது பல்கணப் பற்றுவிடாரே, is hard to join to them: it may say that those who do not let go of the many (senses, people, or goblin hosts) lose all this, or that what is cut away is that attachment. துறை may be ford, path or field.

2646.reading: Once I took in hand the sword the First Lord gave, no one can pierce me or turn me aside; I will test there so that no trace is left; the God of the beginning has become this one.
2646.nuance: The sword is traditionally knowledge given by the Lord or guru; Sengalvaraya compares Arunagirinathar's sword of knowledge-flame in Kandar Alankaram. அவன் இவன் ஆமே may mean the Lord has become the speaker, or simply that this is the primal god. வேதித்து may mean piercing or transforming.

2647.reading: Wasting away that embryo and the formless, the bond of making deeds, fearful servitude and the many births, and setting the mind right: for the skilled who meet that test, it becomes the Supreme itself.
2647.nuance: அந்தக் கருவை யருவை may be 'that embryo, the formless' or a play on கரு and அரு (form and formless). பணியச்சம் may be servitude and fear, or fear that makes one bow. தற்பரம் is the Supreme in itself.

2648.reading: He told me the one thing beyond telling; cutting off the craving for the arts that rose without bound, keeping my wave-like body from leaving me and setting it right, the Supreme entered into me, now flawless.
2648.nuance: கலைவேட்டு may be craving for learning and the arts, or for the kalas, the phases of the yogic breath. திரையொத்த உடல் (body like a wave, or wrinkled) is kept, not discarded: the Lord enters the embodied person.

links.note: 2615 says cut desire even for the Lord; here the creeper reaches the Lord joined with longing (விருப்பொடு கூடி). Read together, longing that seeks the Lord is not the desire 2615 cuts, unless 2640's longing belongs to Uma alone.
2614 says the Lord is in no temple but in the desireless heart; 2641 tells it as experience: Nandi comes and takes the inner self as his temple.

2635 says Nandi danced in the great bliss beyond speech (பேச்சற்ற பேரின்பத்து) and the test is to hide oneself away and stay still. 1595 says that in the great bliss beyond speech (பேச்சற்ற இன்பத்துப் பேரானந்தத்திலே) the Lord made the poet Siva and made him die. Both phrase the bliss the same way and pair it with the self's disappearance.

2637 says no one knows what knowledge and ignorance are, and both are rightly seen when knowledge goes beyond both (அறிவறியாமை கடந்து). 2580 calls for putting away both knowing and not-knowing (அறிவறியாமை இரண்டும் அகற்றி) to grasp the Siva who is dense knowledge. Both set the goal past the pair of knowing and ignorance, not on the side of knowing.

2638 names the goal by negations: the sign that is no sign, the union that does not join, the knowledge that does not know (குறியாக் குறி ... அறியா அறிவு). 2353 says to unite in a way the mark is not known and stay without knowing knowledge (குறிஅறியாவகை கூடுமின் ... அறிவறியா இருந்து). The two use the same terms, குறி, கூடல, அறிவு, each negated, for the same state.

2639 says the Lord is like ghee in milk, juice in fruit and fragrance in the flower (பாலினுள் நெய்யும்), mingled everywhere. 2115 says the Stainless one is there as ghee within milk (நெய்த்தலைப் பால்போல்) yet people do not desire that light. Both use ghee in milk for a presence everywhere but unseen; 2115 adds that people still fail to seek it.

2639 likens the Lord's pervasion to juice in fruit (பழத்துள் இரதமும்). 2831 uses the same phrase (பழத்துள் இரதமும்) for the sweetness of turiya flooding the body. The image is the Lord's hidden presence in one and the felt bliss of the state in the other.

2645 speaks of drawing and striking with the sword of knowledge (ஞானத் துறைவாள் உருவி) to know and join the Lord. 2968 says that if Yama comes the poet will strike him with the sword of knowledge (ஞானவாள் கொண்டே எறிவன்). The same weapon is aimed at the Lord's attainment in one and at death in the other.

2646 says that once the poet took the sword the First Lord gave (ஆதிப்பிரான் தந்த வாள்), no one could turn him aside. 1591 says the Lord, when he gave his feet, gave the strength of knowledge that is a sword (வாள்தந்த ஞான வலி). Both make the sword of knowledge the Lord's gift, not the seeker's own.

2648 says the teacher told the poet the one thing beyond telling (உரையற்றதொன்றை உரைத்தான்), cut the boundless craving (கரையற்றெழுந்த) and entered him. 134 says those who feel beyond words what the teacher of waveless mind speaks (உரையற்று உணர்வோர்) become reality in the shoreless light (கரையற்ற சோதி). Both share உரையற்று and கரையற்ற, and both make the guru's word beyond words the means of union.

source_issues: 2640: line 1 reads விகிர்த்னை, a misprint for விகிர்தனை.
2645: line 2 reads அறிவது னோடேயவ், probably அறிவதனோடே அவ் with a dropped or misplaced syllable.
2646: line 1 reads வாள்ங்கைக்கொண்டபின், a misprint for வாளங்கைக் கொண்டபின்.
